oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Alex (oncall) — cluster="infer-prod-us-west2" severity=P1. Detected repeated GPU driver Xid events and node reboots affecting 3 nodes. Pager: https://console.redwood.example/incidents/1901234567 

alex: ACK. I'm on call. Starting triage now. Which nodes are flapping?

oncall-bot: Nodes flagged in last 10m: infer-gpu-07 (xid_count=14), infer-gpu-12 (xid_count=9), infer-gpu-19 (xid_count=22, last-reset=30s). Autoscaler notices spike in pod restarts on those nodes.

maria: Observed repeated Xid 31 and Xid 79 in kernel logs, plus ECC correctable error counts climbing. Example from infer-gpu-19: ```
Mar 11 03:12:08 infer-gpu-19 kernel: NVRM: Xid (0001:01): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 11 03:12:09 infer-gpu-19 kernel: nvidia: GPU 0000:01:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 11 03:12:09 infer-gpu-19 systemd: containerd: runtime: starting container: fatal: driver reset observed, container OOMs following restart
```

jin: Recommend cordon+drain the two lower-traffic nodes (07,12) immediately and move workloads off 19 for a cleaner restart. Commands: ```
# cordon
kubectl cordon infer-gpu-07
kubectl cordon infer-gpu-12
# safe drain (ignore DaemonSets, force evict best-effort batch jobs)
kubectl drain infer-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --timeout=10m
kubectl drain infer-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --timeout=10m
```

alex: Doing cordon now on 07/12. Jin, are we able to restart driver on 19 without a full reboot? If not, we should migrate traffic and reboot cleanly.

maria: On 19 there's persistent ECC correctables and then a driver watchdog reset. Restarting nvidia driver sometimes helps but we've seen residual state that needs kernel module reload or node reboot. Quick attempt: ```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced || sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia && sudo systemctl restart kubelet
```
Note: coordinate with platform before modprobe on prod nodes.

deploy-bot: Observability note: Model-serving pods on infer-gpu-19 saw token latency spikes and 502s between 03:11-03:14, ~1.2k failed requests. Route fallback to us-east started automatically for autoscaled routes.

lia (support): Customer impact: we have ~6 customers on dedicated pools that had degraded throughput (errors and retries). Top affected: acme-inc (prod), luma-ai (staging). I'll open an outbound with ACME and include the transient nature + mitigation steps. Draft line: "We experienced transient GPU driver resets in us-west which caused some generation requests to fail or time out between 03:10–03:15 UTC. We rerouted traffic and are investigating root cause; we'll update within 2 hours." Thoughts? :speech_balloon:

alex: LGTM, lia. Please include approximate number of failed requests (1.2k) and mention no model data was lost; it's inference runtime failures only. Also add our temporary mitigation (cordon/drain + restart/reboot).

sam: I'm on next shift in ~45m. Alex — can you hand off with runbook + items outstanding? I'll take full ownership after that.

alex: Handoff summary for sam: 
- Current state: infer-gpu-19 quarantined; 07/12 drained and cordoned, pods rescheduled to other nodes/regions.
- Actions taken: cordon+drain 07/12, started safe restart on 19 (driver reload attempted).
- Next actions: if driver reload fails -> reboot node; if reboots continue, cordon remaining nodes and enable region fallback, throttle batch sizes for heavy customers, open hardware ticket for ECC check.
- Oncall playbook link: https://wiki.redwood.example/oncall/runbooks/gpu-driver-xid

maria: After driver reload we still see Xid bursts on 19. Recommend reboot and then run the GPU diagnostics (nvidia-smi -q -d ECC, memtest) and escalate to hardware if ECC correctables keep rising.

alex: Reboot scheduled on infer-gpu-19 in 5m. I'll monitor post-reboot logs. Setting incident tag: type=gpu-driver-xid, severity=p1, impact=partial.

oncall-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigating, assigned=alex, incident_id=INC-1901234567. Notifications sent to #eng-runtime and #customer-impact.

deploy-bot: Suggestion: dynamically lower max_batch_tokens for streaming routes on affected service to reduce memory pressure while nodes recover. Config patch example: ```
PATCH /v1/services/serve/config
{ "max_batch_tokens": 512 }
```

lia (support): Sent initial outbound to ACME with incident summary + mitigation steps. Will post follow-ups after reboot verification.

alex: Reboot complete on infer-gpu-19. Post-reboot logs: ```
Mar 11 03:18:22 infer-gpu-19 kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:01:00: GPU-reset: reset successful
Mar 11 03:18:25 infer-gpu-19 nvidia-smi: ECC errors: correctable=0 uncorrectable=0
Mar 11 03:18:30 kubelet: pods started successfully, no OOMs observed after restart
```

maria: I'm still seeing sporadic Xid 31 traces in dmesg but at low frequency (2 events in 10m). ECC counters look stable. Recommend continue cordon for 30m of stable telemetry before uncordoning.

alex: Agreed. Keeping nodes cordoned until stable. Sam — I'll leave the incident in your queue with checklist: run hardware diag if Xid > 5 in 30m, open support ticket with provider for suspected ECC cell, and create postmortem ticket when we clear P1.

sam: Taking handoff. Thanks Alex. I'll follow up if Xid rates increase. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: from=alex to=sam at=1901234625. Incident remains open: status=monitoring.
